lane: TWO LOW AUDIT FINDINGS — RENDERING / HIT-TESTING (damage-number anchor on a hidden connector; rampAnchorAtPoint vs fog + atlas-load state)
summary: Both findings are STILL LIVE at 7d1514b, and both are render/input-only. FINDING 1: `damageNumbers.ts` imports neither `concealment.ts` nor `towerCover.ts` — it anchors every connector floater at the raw bond midpoint (`damageNumbers.ts:691`, and again at `:660` for the break hit), while `structureRenderer.ts:226` `continue`s on any bond whose cover alpha has ramped to ~0. So the number is anchored to a connector that is provably not drawn. The handoff's phrase "blank ground" is slightly imprecise and I measured it rather than repeating it: on a STAR_R-44 star the bond midpoint is ~22 px from the centroid and `LIFT_PX` is 30, so upper-arm connectors start at cy−52 against an art top of cy−49.5 (goblin, artPx 99) or cy−42 (hub, artPx 84) and then rise another 23 px — those genuinely clear the art into empty sky; lower-arm ones land ON the building but at an arbitrary offset with nothing under them. The substance holds; "over blank ground" is true for roughly the top half of the connectors, not all of them. FINDING 2: `rampAnchorAtPoint` (`structureRamp.ts:545`) iterates `world.creatureSpawners` and `world.defenders` and applies only a geometry test — it never consults `isConcealed`, and it cannot consult the atlas state, which is private to the renderer instance. Its own publisher `StructureRampRenderer.drawStructure` clears TWO gates it does not (`structureRampRenderer.ts:193` fog, `:194` atlas) before committing a sprite. The fog half is a real BUILD-phase information leak: clicking blank fogged ground opens a full "ENEMY BUILDING" card with the recipe name, connector count, shape count and a LIVE health value (`characterSheetModel.ts:1227`, `:1280`). This is a CLASS, not a one-off — `towerAnchorAtPoint` (`towerFrames.ts:410`) and the primitive fallback scan (`controls.ts:832-840`) have the identical hole, and `grep -rn "isConcealed" src/input/` returns nothing at all. No test in the tree pins fog or atlas state against either hit test.

findings.claim: F1 — the connector damage floater is anchored at the raw bond midpoint with no reference to tower cover; damageNumbers.ts imports neither concealment.ts nor towerCover.ts. Still live.
findings.evidence:
track(
        `b:${bond.id}`, bond.damageFifths,
        (a.pos.x + b.pos.x) / 2, (a.pos.y + b.pos.y) / 2,
        a.placedBy, true, false,
      );   — and the file's import block (lines 58-69) contains pixi.js, world.ts, types.ts, gatherer.ts, constants.ts, castleGuns.ts, voltkin-config.ts, defender.ts, stats.ts. No './concealment.ts', no './towerCover.ts'.

findings.claim: F1 — the same raw midpoint is used for the connector-BREAK number, so the swing that snaps an arm also prints at the invisible connector.
F1 — the bond the floater points at is genuinely NOT DRAWN: structureRenderer skips any bond whose cover alpha has ramped below epsilon. This is the other end of the mismatch.
findings.evidence:
const coverAlpha = coverAlphaForBond(bond.id);
      if (coverAlpha <= TOWER_COVER_DRAW_EPSILON) continue;   — preceded at :220 by the S183 note that DAMAGED_BOND_MIN_ALPHA (which existed precisely so 'the floating number appears over a connector the player can actually see') was retired.

findings.claim: F1 — geometry measured, not asserted: the offset that puts the number off the art. LIFT_PX is 30 and the floater then rises RISE_PX_TOTAL 23 more over its life; a star's bond midpoint is STAR_R/2 = 22 px from the centroid; goblin artPx 99 (half 49.5), hub artPx 84 (half 42), and place() puts the art top at cy - 0.5*artPx. Upper-arm connectors therefore start at cy-52, above the art, and rise clear of it.
findings.evidence: const RISE_PX_TOTAL = 23; // 31.25 px/s × 0.75 s   … const LIFT_PX = 30;  (line 130)   — with `src/state/blueprints.ts:138: const STAR_R = 44;` and `src/render/structureRamp.ts:282: export const GOBLIN_TOWER_ART_PX = 99;` / `:243: export const HUB_ART_PX = 84;`

findings.claim: F2 — rampAnchorAtPoint applies a pure geometry test over both collections and never consults fog or atlas state. Still live.
F2 — the renderer that DRAWS these towers clears exactly the two gates the hit test skips, in adjacent lines. This is the authoritative statement of the divergence.

F2 — user-visible symptom: a click in fog opens a full enemy-building card. The card even carries a LIVE health value under a 'LAST SEEN' label — `frozen` styles the bar but does not freeze the number.
findings.evidence: const frozen = isConcealed(prim.pos.x, prim.pos.y, owner);   (line 1227)   …   health: { cur: Math.max(0, pool - banked), max: pool, frozen },   (line 1280)   — `cur` is recomputed every frame from world.bonds; characterSheet.ts:403 renders `if (frozen) this.text('LAST SEEN', …)`.

findings.claim: F2 — the fix is SAFE for the owner's repair gesture, and this is the load-bearing property: isConcealed short-circuits false for your own things before any geometry runs, so a fog gate on the pick can never make your own tower unrepairable.
F2 — it is a CLASS, not a one-off: the race-tower box has the same hole, and the whole input layer is fog-blind. `grep -rn "isConcealed" src/input/` returns zero lines.
F2 — the atlas half of the finding is real but MILD, and its predicate is genuinely unavailable at the call site: `manifests` is private renderer state, and a failed load is never retried.

ADJACENT, in the same blast radius, unreported by the audit: damage numbers themselves have no fog gate. An enemy creature skipped by creatureRenderer's concealment `continue` still prints its damage numbers in plain view during BUILD.
findings.evidence: if (delta > 0) this.emit(world, c.id, c.pos.x, c.pos.y, delta, 'damage', owner);   — with no isConcealed test anywhere in the file, against `src/render/creatureRenderer.ts:497: if (isConcealed(creature.pos.x, creature.pos.y, creature.ownerPlayerId)) continue;`. I did NOT verify how much combat occurs while fogActive (networked && PLAYING && BUILD, vision.ts:174), so I am reporting the code shape, not a measured in-match symptom.

fix_shape:
TWO INDEPENDENT EDITS. They share no file and can ship separately.

F2 (the one I would do first — smaller, and it closes a leak):
· `src/render/structureRamp.ts` — `rampAnchorAtPoint`, inside `consider()`, after `rampMembersAt` resolves: one `if (isConcealed(anchor.pos.x, anchor.pos.y, anchor.placedBy)) return;` on the ANCHOR primitive, matching `structureRampRenderer.ts:193` field-for-field. That is one import + 2 lines. ⚠ It makes a pure geometry function depend on the module-level concealment frame; the alternative (take a `concealed: (x,y,owner)=>boolean` predicate parameter, defaulted) keeps the function pure and testable and costs one more line at `controls.ts:824`. I prefer the parameter form — `structureRamp.ts` currently has no render-state import at all, and the whole S183 test file drives it as a pure function.
· `src/render/towerFrames.ts:410` — the identical 2 lines in `towerAnchorAtPoint`, or the leak just moves to the twelve race towers.
· OPTIONALLY `src/input/controls.ts:832-840` — the primitive fallback scan, same gate. Doing 545 and 410 without 832 leaves the leak at reduced radius (a ~14-17 px dot per shape instead of a 99 px box), which is a real reduction but not a close.
· The atlas half: there is a clean existing signal and no new plumbing needed — cover is published ONLY after both gates pass (`structureRampRenderer.ts:223`), so a `towerCover.ts` export of "is this prim currently marked" (the `current.prims` set, ~4 lines) is a single predicate that covers fog AND atlas together. ⚠ It inverts during the crumble reveal (cover stops arriving), so the art box would go dead exactly while the tower is falling — acceptable only because the shapes are visible again by then and the `controls.ts:832` fallback picks them up. I would NOT take this unless the owner wants the atlas half closed; the fog gate alone is the value.
Total F2: ~10-15 lines across 2-3 files.

F1 — the shape depends entirely on the owner's answer below.
· SUPPRESS: `src/render/damageNumbers.ts`, import `coverAlphaForBond` + `TOWER_COVER_DRAW_EPSILON`, and skip the emit at `:660` and the `track` at `:689` when the bond is covered. ~6 lines, 1 file. Micro.
· RE-ANCHOR onto the building: needs `towerCover.ts` to remember the covering structure's CENTROID per covered bond. All four publish sites (`structureRampRenderer.ts:223`, `towerRenderer.ts:313`, `voltkinTowerRenderer.ts:576`, and the `markTowerCover` signature at `towerCover.ts:203`) already hold a centroid at the call — `drawStructure` destructures `cx, cy` from `rampMembersAt` two lines earlier. So: a 4th arg on `markTowerCover`, a `Map<BondId,{x,y}>`, one exported lookup, and damageNumbers substitutes it for the midpoint. ~30-40 lines across 5 files. Standard, and it touches the three-publish-site contract that `towerCover.test.ts` counts.
four_sites_risk:
NONE. Neither finding touches factory / serialize / hash / worker, and neither needs a PROTOCOL_VERSION bump (47 stands).
· Everything involved lives in `src/render/` and `src/input/` and is a read-only consumer of `World`. `rampAnchorAtPoint` takes `world` and returns a `PrimitiveId | null`; `damageNumbers` never writes `world` (its own docblock, line ~40: "this is a renderer-local visual over synced state: it cannot desync the sim, and `world` is never written to").
· No new serialized field is required by either fix. The centroid a re-anchor would need is DERIVED per frame from `Primitive.pos`, which is already a required wire field — the same argument `towerCover.ts` makes for itself ("costs no sim state, no snapshot bytes and no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump").
· TWO determinism hazards that are NOT four-sites but must be respected:
  1. `damageAnchor` (`damageNumbers.ts:348`) keeps an explicit total order — squared distance then `(o.id as number) < bestId` — with a docblock naming the S155 melee defect. Any edit to the anchor path must preserve it: two peers watch the same floater.
  2. `towerCover` is tick-driven on purpose ("NO WALL CLOCK … a tick-driven ramp means they watch the same thing", towerCover.ts docblock). A centroid added to it must come from the publisher's synced `Primitive.pos` walk, never from Pixi sprite bounds, or the two peers' floaters diverge. The same rule `controls.ts` already states for every pick ("`bag.pos` and `bag.radius`, never sprite bounds").
· One NON-determinism hazard worth naming for F2: `isConcealed` is per-VIEWER by construction (it reads `ctx.localPlayerId`). Putting it inside `rampAnchorAtPoint` makes that function's answer viewer-dependent. That is correct — it is a click target, not sim state — but it means the function can no longer be described as "pure" in its docblock, and the docblock currently opens with "PURE —". That line must change in the same commit or the canon rots.
tests_owed:
F2:
· `src/render/structureRamp.test.ts` — the existing `structureWorld()` helper builds a bare cast object with no `localPlayerId`, `gameState` or `matchPhase`, so `fogActive` is false and every existing case stays green unchanged. New cases need a world where `fogActive` is true and the anchor is out of vision: assert `rampAnchorAtPoint` returns null for an ENEMY tower in fog, and — the case that matters most — assert it still returns the anchor for the LOCAL player's tower in fog (the `owner === ctx.localPlayerId` short-circuit at `concealment.ts:107`). Without that second assertion the fix can silently recreate "an invisible tower is an unrepairable tower", which is the exact outcome the function exists to prevent.
· `resetConcealmentForTest()` (`concealment.ts:118`) in `afterEach`, or one spec leaks a context into the next — the file says so.
· A mirror pair in `towerFrames.test.ts` for `towerAnchorAtPoint`.
· ⛔ A SOURCE-TEXT GUARD IS NOT ENOUGH HERE, and this repo has the scar: S182's cost-plate tripwire was green while the bug shipped twice, because it proved a line EXISTED and not that it was REACHED. The assertion must call `rampAnchorAtPoint` with a live concealment context and read the return value.

F1:
· `damageNumbers.test.ts` / `damageNumbersLifecycle.test.ts` — with `beginTowerCoverFrame` + `markTowerCover` applied to the bond, assert either (suppress) that no floater is created, or (re-anchor) that the floater's anchor equals the structure centroid and NOT the bond midpoint. `__resetTowerCoverForTests()` (`towerCover.ts:258`) in `afterEach`.
· `towerCover.test.ts` already counts the publish sites and the cover-alpha CONSUMERS and pins both totals (stated in the `towerCover.ts` docblock). A re-anchor adds a consumer and changes `markTowerCover`'s arity — both totals must be re-pinned in the same commit, and the 4-arg call must land at all four publish sites or the fix is three-quarters done, which is this project's named failure mode.
· ⭐ Whichever way F1 goes, apply the S184 mutation lesson: revert the guard, require a captured RED, restore byte-identical. A floater-position assertion is exactly the kind that can pass against the old behaviour if it is written loosely.
owner_questions: F1 — SUPPRESS or RE-ANCHOR? This is a genuine conflict between two of his own rulings, not a taste call. S175 P9: "you gotta see damage everywhere, not just on characters" (quoted at damageNumbers.ts:~416). R183-E, S183: "you can see the tower is damaged. You can just click the tower and repair it. You don't have to see the connectors" — and that ruling is what retired DAMAGED_BOND_MIN_ALPHA, whose ENTIRE stated purpose was "the floating number appears over a connector the player can actually see" (SPARK_CANON.md:351). Suppressing is ~6 lines in one file; re-anchoring onto the building is ~35 lines across the four markTowerCover publish sites. One sentence from him decides which.

F2 — should a fogged enemy structure be CLICKABLE AT ALL, or clickable-but-frozen? The card the click opens is not blank: it prints the recipe name, CONNECTORS, SHAPES, and a health value recomputed live every frame under a "LAST SEEN" label (characterSheetModel.ts:1227/:1280, characterSheet.ts:403). His fog spec is "I shouldn't see their buildings, their sparks, their spawn, their connectors" (quoted verbatim at concealment.ts:~93). But the `frozen` plumbing exists precisely so a card SURVIVES its subject going into fog — so the design may be that you keep a card you already opened, and only the NEW pick should be gated. Those are different fixes.
size_estimate: Standard (10-30K) — and it SPLITS cleanly into two Micros if he wants them separately. F2's fog gate alone is a genuine Micro (~10-15 lines, 2-3 files: structureRamp.ts, towerFrames.ts, optionally controls.ts) plus two test files. F1 is a Micro if he rules SUPPRESS (6 lines, 1 file) and Standard if he rules RE-ANCHOR, because that changes markTowerCover's arity and therefore visits all four publish sites plus the two counts towerCover.test.ts pins. I would price the batch as Standard on the assumption that at least one arm is the re-anchor, and because the tests are the larger half of the work in both arms.
